rules.definition: A pedestrian on the carriageway outside a crossing.
rules.rule: Ground point of a walking person (riders removed) inside the hand-drawn carriageway, ≥ 0.8 % of the frame from the kerb, ≥ 3 % away from every crossing and outside the bus-stop bay, for ≥ 1.2 s while moving ≥ 2 % of the frame. Segments of the same class closer than 2 s are merged.

rules.definition: A vehicle drives through a crossing while a pedestrian is on it or stepping onto it.
rules.rule: A motor vehicle passes through a crossing polygon in ≤ 6 s at walking speed or faster, while a moving pedestrian is on the same crossing (not at its kerb ends) within 10 % of the frame for ≥ 2 samples. Segment = vehicle enters → leaves.

rules.definition: A vehicle crosses the stop line while its signal is red.
rules.rule: Front of the vehicle (bottom of the box) crosses the near-arm stop line while the lamp reads red, ≥ 0.8 s after red onset and ≥ 3 s before it ends, then enters the junction. Ignored when ≥ 3 vehicles cross within ±2 s (a platoon means the approach really has green).

rules.definition: A vehicle stops past the stop line on red without entering the junction.
rules.rule: Vehicle stationary for ≥ 2 s between the stop line (≥ 1.2 % past it) and the far edge of the crossing while the lamp is red. Segment = vehicle stops → signal turns green.

rules.definition: A vehicle stationary on the carriageway for ≥ 10 s, not in a queue at a signal.
rules.rule: Car / bus / truck stationary ≥ 10 s on the carriageway; excluded in the signal approach, inside the junction for < 45 s (waiting to turn), at crossings, at the frame border, buses in the bus bay, and when another slow vehicle's box is within 3.5 % of the frame for most of the stop (queue).

rules.definition: Traffic at a standstill or crawling across all lanes of a direction.
rules.rule: ≥ 6 vehicles in the approach or the far carriageway with median speed < 0.1 box-heights/s and > 80 % of them slow, for ≥ 12 s, only while the boulevard signal is green (a red queue is not congestion); buses in the bus bay are ignored.

rules.definition: A vehicle moves against the traffic direction of its lane.
rules.rule: Moving vehicle whose heading is opposite (cos < −0.6) to the learned flow field in coherent cells (resultant length > 0.85, ≥ 25 samples) outside the junction box, for ≥ 1.5 s and ≥ 5 % of the frame.

findings: The four clips are 4K (3840×2160) at 29.97 fps, not 25 fps: every time value in the pipeline is derived from the file's own fps.

The framing moves by up to 3.4 % of the frame between clips (the tripod was re-positioned), so a layout drawn once would miss the crossings by up to 130 px in 4K. We register every video to one canonical frame (SIFT + RANSAC, 160–3,000 inliers per clip).
Two clips are at dusk and two are sunny midday footage with hard shadows. In sunlight the lit signal lamp is dim (≈ 30 levels of redness instead of ≈ 220), so lamp scores are normalised per clip.
The boulevard signal cycles every ≈ 77–80 s (≈ 38 s red, ≈ 38 s green) in all clips; the phase reading lets rules separate a red queue from congestion, and a stop-line violation from a normal stop.
Pedestrians often leave crossing A early and cut diagonally across the junction to the triangle island: the heatmap shows this path. This is the main source of jaywalking segments.
When the junction is blocked (C3905, 1:18–1:56) the approach queue stops on crossing A during red while people walk between the cars: a stop-line violation, not a red-light run.
COCO detectors see white-painted tree trunks as people and riders as pedestrians. We drop persons that never move and persons that overlap a bicycle / motorcycle for most of their track.
report:
What we built

A one-command pipeline (python run_submission.py --videos DIR) that registers each video to a canonical view, tracks road users with YOLO11s + ByteTrack at 7.5 fps, reads the boulevard signal from the lamp pixels, and turns tracks into events with seven geometric rules. Part B runs a lighter causal tracker and scores time-to-collision between road users.

What worked

  • Reading the signal from pixels. The lamp on the median tip is visible in every clip; with per-clip normalisation it gives a clean red/green phase even in glare. Without it red_light, stop_line and congestion would be guesses.
  • Registration. One layout, four framings; the warped daylight clips line up with the dusk reference to a few pixels.
  • Ground points in canonical coordinates + speeds in box heights per second. One stationarity threshold works from the foreground to the far carriageway.
  • Precision over coverage. The metric averages F1 over every class we predict, so we only predict classes we can check.

What did not work (or not yet)

  • Accidents and near misses. None of the sample clips contain one, so we could not tune a detector for them. Part A leaves both classes out; Part B anticipates accidents from time-to-collision, but its calibration is a design choice, not a measurement.
  • Jaywalking boundaries. People who walk just beside a crossing are ambiguous; our 3 % buffer is a judgement call and the largest source of disagreement with our own labels.
  • Daylight signal. In glare the phase switch is detected up to ~3 s late, so we ignore red-light crossings in the last 3 s of a red phase and platoons of ≥ 3 vehicles.
  • Only one stop line is observable (the near arm). Red-light running on the other approaches happens outside the frame.
  • Turns (illegal_turn, illegal_u_turn) and solid-line crossings need lane-level markings; we have not mapped the lanes.

What we would do next

  • Fine-tune the detector on a few hundred frames of this camera (small, far pedestrians at the bus stop are missed at dusk).
  • Map lanes and turn permissions to add illegal_turn / illegal_u_turn / solid_line_crossing.
  • Train a clip classifier on DoTA / CCD for accident and near-miss confirmation and calibrate Part B on it.
  • Label more of the footage to tune thresholds per class instead of by inspection.

signal_note: red = boulevard stopped, green = boulevard moving. The cycle is stable at ≈ 77–80 s.

failures.note: Occlusion: a bus hides the far crossing; we flagged a car whose pedestrians were still on the kerb. Not in our labels (false positive).
Pedestrians waiting at the kerb of crossing B look ‘on the crossing’ from this angle; the car passes them without a conflict (false positive).
Far refuge island: at 40 px tall, 10 px of foot position decides kerb vs. road. We now ignore people under 4.5 % of the frame height, which also drops some true cases far away.
Blocked junction at dusk: the queue stands on crossing A for 40 s while people weave between cars. We report one long stop_line segment; annotators might split it or call part of it congestion.

dev.intro: We labelled the sample clips ourselves with the organisers' start/end conventions (95 segments). C3905 and C3902 were labelled by watching the clips and checking every candidate from a deliberately loose version of our rules; C3897 and C3896 only by verifying our own detections frame by frame, so on those two clips the table measures precision, not recall. The labels share our blind spots: treat these numbers as a sanity check, not a test-set estimate. Scores are the official evaluate.py run on predictions_samples.json.
